free_text.inst.v2.D8: One reads it as one reads a great many things put before one: with interest, and without letting it settle the day. It is right about my father, and about luck and standing, and I was struck that it should single those out as the unusual notes; my father was the making of me, and what standing I have came from the position rather than from anything I did to seek it. It is right too that partnership has read well. I was married for seventy-three years and it was the whole steadiness of my life. Where it seems to me wide of the mark is in temperament. It calls me sociable and drawn to comfort and beauty and good company. I am fond of dogs and horses and of Scotland, and I like people very much, but I am not what anyone would call an easy or expansive person, and comfort has never been the point. Duty was the point. It says spending and time away from home read hard, and there I would simply say the opposite: the travelling was among the best of it, and one of the few parts of the work I could do that no one else could. Income and friends it calls hard, and I have wanted for neither. The document is honest enough to say that most of it would fit most people, which I thought creditable, and I would rather that plainly said than dressed up. Much of it was left blank, so one could not judge it fairly on the whole. I am content not to know what is coming, and never much cared to be told.

notes: Answered in character as Elizabeth II (b. 21 April 1926, 02:40, 17 Bruton Street, London; d. 2022), having first read the prepared reading. Biography takes precedence where it conflicts with the reading (temperament, travel, income). A36 asks about mid-2023 onward, which postdates her death; answered 'same' as a neutral placeholder rather than left blank. A13 answered 'lost' (Princess Margaret, d. 2002) though the relationship was close. A14 'none' reflects private tutoring with no formal schooling or qualifications. A17 'own' reflects that she had no employer or senior; A19 'above' reflects her own characteristic modesty about recognition. C6 read as the constraint of the role rather than literal institutional confinement. D4 lists chapters that were absent or empty in the supplied reading.
